pathway.title: Bausch & Lomb Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage has fallen but remains high, and it fell because earnings rose, not because debt fell. Total debt of USD 5,095 million is 6.47x last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 787 million, against 9.52x at FY2025, while debt itself is higher than at FY2025. EBITDA rose 47.38%, but USD 62 million of non-cash inventory step-up amortization sat in the FY2025 base, so the like-for-like rise is 32.05%. Because leverage is a ratio to one year of earnings, a return of EBITDA to its FY2025 level, a fall of 32.15%, would put total debt at 9.54x EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C18

- Interest cover is thin and the debt is mostly floating, so a rate shock and an earnings shock would arrive together. Accrued interest of USD 383 million takes 48.67% of EBITDA, cash interest cover was 1.41x in FY2025 and cannot be measured for the latest twelve months, and 72.12% of principal pays a floating rate with no interest rate swap or cap described in the filings. A rise of 100 bp adds about USD 36.53 million a year and takes cover from 2.05x to 1.88x; at the FY2025 earnings level cover would be 1.39x, or 1.27x after the same rise. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 219; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 102; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C19; calculation C20

- Cash conversion has turned positive but is still modest. Last-twelve-month free cash flow of USD 252 million is 32.02% of EBITDA and 4.95% of total debt, after deficits of USD 198 million, USD 59 million and USD 66 million in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025. Trade receivables absorbed USD 496 million over those three years, more than the cumulative deficit of USD 323 million, so working capital, not the operating margin alone, decides whether the recovery in free cash flow lasts. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C28; calculation C29

- Liquidity is adequate for the next year, and the pressure sits in 2028 and 2031. Liquidity of USD 1,179 million is 3.30x the USD 357 million of fourth-quarter needs the issuer lists. Nothing but amortization is due before 2028, when USD 1,440 million falls due, 28.43% of principal and 1.83x EBITDA; USD 3,434 million, 67.80% of principal and 4.36x EBITDA, falls due in 2031. At the FY2025 earnings level those multiples would be 2.70x and 6.43x, so the 2028 notes are the first test of market access and the swing factor from 2027. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C45; calculation C43; calculation C41; calculation C44; calculation C42; calculation C21; calculation C22

- The revolver covenant is dormant and leaves room, but it is the only maintenance test and its headroom cannot be measured. The first lien net leverage test of 5.75x, stepping down to 5.50x, 5.25x and then 5.00x in later periods, applies only when revolver loans exceed 35% of the USD 800 million commitment, that is USD 280 million; USD 100 million is drawn, 12.50% of commitments, leaving USD 180 million before the test applies. Even if the USD 85 million acquisition and the USD 75 million executive payment were both drawn in full, loans would be USD 260 million, USD 20 million below the line, so the test is unlikely to apply in the fourth quarter but headroom beyond that is thin, and the issuer states compliance without a ratio so the result of a test is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C48; calculation C49; calculation C52; calculation C50; calculation C51

- Control by the parent is the main non-financial risk and has a direct liquidity link. Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, and part of its holding is pledged in a subsidiary for that subsidiary's 10.00% notes due 2032, in an amount the filings do not state. A change of control would let holders of both secured notes require repurchase at 101% of principal, USD 2,186.65 million before accrued interest or 1.85x liquidity; whether the credit agreement carries a comparable trigger is not stated, so the exposure of the largest debt, the term loan, is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; calculation C46; calculation C47

- Pricing and rebates carry the revenue base and are exposed to regulation and generic entry. Net pricing contributed USD 128 million of the USD 317 million nine-month revenue increase and volume USD 139 million, but deductions from gross product sales rose 3.2 percentage points to 39.5% in 2025 and were 38.4% in the nine months of 2026 against 39.1% a year earlier, and a settlement with a generic maker allows entry for Lumify drops from 2027-06-30 or earlier. The ten largest products were 56% of 2025 revenue, up from 48% in 2023, and Lumify revenue is not stated, so the size of the 2027 exposure is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C37; calculation C54

- The recovery leans on Pharmaceuticals and on a depressed 2025 base. Pharmaceuticals supplied 56.31% of the USD 293 million rise in nine-month segment profit, helped by lower launch spending and the end of XIIDRA inventory step-up, and Surgical went from USD 3 million to USD 58 million with premium lens growth and the 2025 enVista recall dropping out of the comparison. These are base effects and launch maturity, so the nine-month gain should not be extrapolated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation C16; calculation C15

- Supply and quality concentrations are tail risks that have so far been contained. Finished product for six named products comes from a single source and about 37% of product sales are made wholly or partly by third parties, and a September 2026 FDA warning letter covers the Tampa site without requiring manufacturing to stop; management expects no supply interruption, a statement the filings do not test. A supply failure would remove revenue from products with no second source and would fall on a cost base the analysis treats as largely fixed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65

cells.text: A global eye-health company founded in 1853 with about 400 products sold in about 100 countries and about 13,000 employees; three reportable segments: Vision Care, Pharmaceuticals and Surgical
One sector, but diversified by segment, product and country inside it; the credit does not rest on a single product line
USD 5,101 million: Vision Care USD 2,923 million (57%), Pharmaceuticals USD 1,284 million (25%), Surgical USD 894 million (18%)
Vision Care carries more than half of revenue and USD 849 million of USD 1,125 million segment profit, so the credit rests on contact lenses and consumer eye care

2023, 2024, 2025: Vision Care USD 689 million, USD 808 million, USD 849 million; Pharmaceuticals USD 241 million, USD 256 million, USD 258 million; Surgical USD 50 million, USD 44 million, USD 18 million. Nine months 2026 against 2025: Vision Care USD 675 million against USD 602 million; Pharmaceuticals USD 289 million against USD 124 million; Surgical USD 58 million against USD 3 million
Pharmaceuticals and Surgical recovered in 2026 from low bases; Surgical earned a 2.01% margin in 2025

McKesson and Cardinal Health each about 10% of 2025 and 2024 revenue, none at 10% in 2023; sales go through wholesalers, retailers and eye care practices; the two largest wholesalers were about 15% of net trade receivables at 2025-12-31
Two wholesalers are about 20% of revenue, so a change in their terms would move working capital
Deductions took 39.5% of gross product sales of USD 8,393 million in 2025 against 36.3% in 2024, mainly rebates on the dry-eye portfolio; 38.4% in nine months 2026 against 39.1%
Net price depends on rebate estimates, USD 556 million accrued at 2025-12-31; the auditor named Medicaid rebates its critical audit matter

25 manufacturing facilities in 11 countries; about 37% of 2025 product sales were produced wholly or partly by third parties; finished product for six named products and active ingredient for four are single-sourced; Tampa received an FDA warning letter in September 2026
A supplier or site failure can stop a named product line; the Tampa matter is the current test

United States and Puerto Rico USD 2,546 million of 2025 revenue (49.91%), China USD 358 million, Russia USD 148 million (2.90%); revenue is weighted to the second half; net receivables from twelve weak-credit countries were USD 139 million at 2025-12-31
Half of revenue is earned in dollars; the rest carries currency, sanction and collection risk and cash timing swings within the year

About 900 research staff and more than 60 projects, research and development USD 371 million in 2025 (7.27% of revenue); the top ten products were 56% of 2025 revenue against 48% in 2023; the PreserVision method patent expired in early 2026 and the product was about 6% of revenue
Concentration in ten products is rising; the company says over-the-counter exclusivity loss is milder than for a branded drug but cannot size it

runs.text: Five strengths and five weaknesses carry the view, each ranked by its weight in the credit judgement.

- Strength 1: earnings and cash flow have recovered. Last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 787 million compares with USD 534 million for FY2025, a like-for-like rise of 32.05% after the inventory step-up charge is removed from the base, and free cash flow of USD 252 million follows three years of deficits. Free cash flow now exceeds the term loan amortization of USD 28 million a year several times over, which lowers the chance that the revolver funds interest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C14

- Strength 2: liquidity and the maturity profile give time. Liquidity of USD 1,179 million is 3.30x the fourth-quarter needs the issuer lists, nothing but amortization falls due before 2028, and the revolver runs to 2030, so a refinancing event is not forced inside the next 12 months and the revolver test applies only above USD 280 million of loans. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C45; calculation C48

- Strength 3: the operating base has three segments and none shrank. In 2025 Vision Care earned USD 2,923 million of revenue, Pharmaceuticals USD 1,284 million and Surgical USD 894 million, and revenue grew in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025, so a setback in one product line does not by itself threaten debt service, although the ten largest products are 56% of revenue. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Strength 4: price and volume both added to growth. In nine months net pricing added USD 128 million and volume USD 139 million to revenue, which shows demand holding at higher prices and supports margin recovery, provided rebates stay contained. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C36; calculation C37

- Strength 5: the parent has so far left cash in the issuer. No dividend has been paid since the listing and related-party charges were USD 8 million in 2025, which means no recurring leakage to the parent appears in the record, although control remains a risk. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 263; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 264

- Weakness 1: leverage is high and interest cover is thin. Total debt is 6.47x EBITDA and accrued interest takes 48.67% of EBITDA, so the issuer has little room if earnings slip, and cash interest cover was 1.41x in FY2025. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7

- Weakness 2: the parent controls the issuer and part of its stake is pledged. A foreclosure or private sale could bring a new controller, and holders of both secured notes could then demand USD 2,186.65 million, 1.85x liquidity. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; calculation C46; calculation C47

- Weakness 3: the maturities are concentrated and mostly floating. USD 1,440 million falls due in 2028 and USD 3,434 million in 2031, 67.80% of principal, while 72.12% of principal pays a floating rate, so refinancing terms and rate moves land on the same debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C44; calculation C3

- Weakness 4: revenue depends on pricing and on products near loss of exclusivity. Deductions from gross sales were 39.5% in 2025, up 3.2 percentage points, net pricing was 40.38% of nine-month growth, and Lumify faces generic entry from 2027-06-30 or earlier. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C54; calculation C39

- Weakness 5: supply and quality are concentrated. Six named products depend on a single finished-product source and Surgical earned only USD 18 million of segment profit in 2025, so a quality event reaches earnings quickly. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64

cells.text: Bausch + Lomb Corporation, a Canadian company with its head office in Vaughan, Ontario; shares trade on the NYSE and TSX as BLCO since 2022-05-06; large accelerated filer; reports in US dollars
The reporting entity is the listed company and its subsidiaries, not the parent

Bausch Health Companies Inc. holds 310,449,643 shares, about 87% at 2026-10-21 (86.84% of 357,497,374 shares), about 88% at 2026-02-11 and 88.1% at 2025-02-12; the parent's share count did not change, the percentage fell as the issuer issued shares
Control is unchanged; all other holders together hold 13.16%

The parent can elect and remove directors and generally decide mergers, financing and dividend policy; until it holds under 50% of the votes the issuer needs its written consent for certain significant actions; the issuer qualifies for controlled-company exemptions
Creditors cannot count on the board to resist the parent on strategy, distributions or acquisitions while control lasts

Nine named independent directors, some of whom also sit on the parent's board; the parent's chief executive has been chairman since August 2026 and interim chief executive since 2026-10-12; the former chief executive left on 2026-10-12
The issuer has no chief executive independent of the parent

Announced 2020-08-06; a distribution depends on the parent reaching targeted debt leverage ratios; the outside date of 2024-12-31 passed without termination; a sale or a transfer to the parent's shareholders is also possible
Ownership could change in a form and on a timetable creditors do not control
A portion of the parent's holding sits in an indirect subsidiary and is pledged for that subsidiary's 10.00% senior secured notes due 2032; the amount is not stated
A default there could force a sale of control; both secured notes carry a 101% repurchase right on a change of control
No dividend declared or paid since the 2022 listing; four holders of record at 2026-02-11
No cash has gone to shareholders since the listing; the credit documents restrict dividends
PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, auditor since 2020, unqualified opinion on the 2025 statements and effective internal control over financial reporting; critical audit matter: Medicaid rebates
The statements are audited and the rebate estimate is the main judgement

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No single transaction sits at the centre of this credit. The open transaction is the separation from Bausch Health, announced on 2020-08-06 and not completed: a distribution depends on the parent reaching leverage targets that the filings do not state, the parent can end the arrangement at its sole discretion, the agreement's outside date of 2024-12-31 passed without termination, and a sale or a transfer to the parent's shareholders remains possible. No date is given. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

The one large acquisition since the listing was XIIDRA from Novartis, signed on 2023-06-30 and completed on 2023-09-29 for USD 1,750 million upfront plus potential milestones of up to USD 750 million, paid from USD 1,400 million of 8.375% secured notes due October 2028 and a new term loan. Later deals were small: Whitecap Biosciences for about USD 28 million on 2025-01-03, two acquisitions for about USD 33 million in November 2025 and Mexican manufacturing assets for about USD 75 million on 2025-12-09. On 2026-10-08 the issuer agreed to buy ophthalmic surgical manufacturing businesses for about USD 85 million of upfront cash, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026; the filings do not name the target, size it or state how the cash will be funded. The separation agreement with the former chief executive adds a lump-sum payment of about USD 75 million, payable under that agreement. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 265; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 266; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 269–270; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89

New debt issues since the listing have been refinancings. On 2022-05-10 the issuer took a USD 2,500 million term loan and a USD 500 million revolver; the term loan proceeds and cash paid the parent USD 2,429 million. It added USD 1,400 million of secured notes and USD 500 million of term loans on 2023-09-29 to buy XIIDRA and USD 400 million of term loans on 2024-11-01. On 2025-06-26 it replaced the 2027 maturities with a USD 800 million revolver due 2030, a USD 2,325 million term loan due 2031 and EUR 675 million of floating rate notes due 2031, and on 2026-01-02 it refinanced the 2028 and 2031 term loans into a USD 2,802 million term loan due 2031-01-15 to extend maturities and lower the rate. At 2026-09-30 principal outstanding was USD 5,065 million, or USD 5,017 million net of USD 48 million of unamortized discounts and issuance costs: the term loan USD 2,788 million, the 2028 notes USD 1,400 million, the 2031 notes USD 765 million, the revolver USD 100 million and other debt USD 12 million. The credit facilities and both note series are secured by the same first-priority liens, the notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the credit agreement and carry a 101% repurchase right on a change of control, and the revolver has a springing first lien net leverage test of 5.75x stepping down to 5.00x that applies only when more than 35% of the USD 800 million commitments are drawn. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 178; 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 258; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 191–192; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C33

fields.value: Bausch & Lomb Corp (reporting as Bausch + Lomb Corporation and its subsidiaries; issuer id blco-1860742), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. fields.value: The sources support a creditor view of Bausch + Lomb's debt, liquidity and operating results to 2026-09-30, but not of covenant headroom or security terms, so leverage must be computed from the statements and legal conclusions stay conditional.

fields.value: - Leverage and covenant headroom cannot be taken from the issuer. No filing prints a figure for EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or free cash flow, the only adjusted measure being constant-currency revenue, and the revolver's springing first lien net leverage test is printed as thresholds of 5.75x stepping down to 5.00x that apply only when loans exceed 35% of commitments, with compliance stated but no ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Claims outside the debt figure are only partly current. Operating lease liabilities of USD 163 million at 2025-12-31 sit outside the balance-sheet debt lines, USD 34 million of failed sale-leaseback obligations sit inside them and had grown to USD 78 million by 2026-09-30, and capital commitments were about USD 128 million at 2025-12-31. The quarterly reports carry no lease or pension note, so these items are nine months older than the debt table. A receivables sale arrangement raised USD 26 million in the nine months and nothing was outstanding at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Legal and market inputs for structure and pricing are missing. No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, and the filings only summarise the financing documents. They give an aggregate fair value of debt of USD 5,091 million at 2026-09-30 and name an equity peer group, but no instrument-level quote, valuation or peer financials, so Legal & covenants, Security selection and Recovery & fulcrum would be conditional on those documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ratings and outlooks of three agencies are printed as of 2026-10-28 although the run supplies none; the Moody's row shows one rating only, so whether it is the corporate or the secured rating is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against calling the requested work ready is that the missing items are the ones a credit committee relies on: the covenant ratio with its definition of earnings, and the lien, guarantee and call terms in the executed debt documents. The revolver test springs only when loans exceed 35% of the USD 800 million commitments, so the test binds only once borrowings pass that level, but the definition of earnings decides when that point is reached, and a filing's summary can omit baskets and definitions. Any covenant or security conclusion should therefore stay conditional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve to ready for Legal & covenants and Covenant capacity if the credit agreement and the indentures were supplied, and for Earnings changes and Earnings quality if a third-quarter earnings release or lender presentation printing adjusted EBITDA were supplied. It would weaken if a filing dated after 2026-10-28 restated figures, closed the acquisition on different terms or changed the revolver.

fields.value: Leverage fell to 6.47x total debt and 5.82x net debt to LTM reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, from 9.52x and 8.80x at FY2025, but cash interest cover cannot be measured for the latest twelve months, so the improvement is unproven against debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The improvement comes from USD 253 million more LTM EBITDA, not from debt reduction, because total debt rose to USD 5,095 million from USD 5,082 million. FY2025 cash interest cover was 1.41x. Cash and revolver availability of USD 1,179 million cover the fourth-quarter cash needs the company states, about USD 357 million, and nothing but amortization falls due before 2028. fields.value: - Leverage fell because earnings rose, not because debt fell. Reported EBITDA, which the issuer does not state and which is built here as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, was USD 787 million for the last twelve months against USD 534 million for FY2025, while total debt moved from USD 5,082 million to USD 5,095 million. Nine-month operating income was USD 271 million against USD 1 million a year earlier, on revenue of USD 4,013 million against USD 3,696 million, and USD 62 million of non-cash inventory step-up amortization sat in the 2025 comparison period while the 2026 statement prints none, so about USD 62 million of the rise is the end of a non-cash charge and not operating improvement.

On accrued interest expense, which the quarterly statements do print, LTM EBITDA covers USD 383 million of expense 2.05x against 1.27x in FY2025; that is a labelled proxy, not the method's measure.

fields.value: - Cash conversion improved with earnings. Operating cash flow was 72.57% of nine-month reported EBITDA against 45.51% a year earlier, and capital expenditure was 5.63% of nine-month revenue against 7.39%.

fields.value: - Liquidity covers the stated near-term needs. Cash of USD 513 million plus USD 666 million of revolver availability, after USD 100 million of borrowings and USD 34 million of letters of credit, is USD 1,179 million against USD 1,047 million at FY2025. The company states fourth-quarter 2026 cash needs of about USD 357 million, being interest of about USD 130 million, amortization of USD 7 million, capital expenditure of about USD 60 million, the USD 85 million acquisition and the USD 75 million executive payment, so liquidity is about 3.30x those needs.

The weighted average stated interest rate is 7.63% and the revolver of USD 800 million matures in 2030.

fields.value: - Reported EBITDA is unadjusted. Adding that back, a house sensitivity labelled Analyst Judgement and applied in no ratio, would lift LTM EBITDA to USD 914 million and cut total leverage to 5.57x. The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA, so no issuer-adjusted figure or bridge exists to show beside it.

Cash interest paid has differed from accrued expense by USD 16 million to USD 45 million in each of the last three years, in both directions, so the proxy of 2.05x is a guide and not a measure.

fields.value: - Cash interest paid for the nine-month 2025 and 2026 periods, and therefore for the last twelve months, is not printed in the quarterly reports; it restricts cash-basis interest cover to full years and leaves the latest period without a measure. fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lease, pension and commitment figures exist only at 2025-12-31 because the quarterly reports carry no such notes, so the claims outside debt are nine months older than the debt figures. Severity Medium; the action is management's quarterly figures for these claims.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The carrying value of the euro floating rate notes in euro is not printed, only the US dollar translation, so the carrying value cell for that instrument is not supplied. Severity Low; the action is the issuer's euro carrying amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - A discrete third-quarter income statement is printed but discrete quarters of depreciation and cash flow are not, so no discrete quarter is carried and nine-month columns stand in. Severity Low; the action is a release stating third-quarter depreciation and cash flow.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bausch & Lomb Corp (reporting as Bausch + Lomb Corporation and its subsidiaries; issuer id blco-1860742), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, ownership, governance, history and sponsor-conduct facts that bear on creditors, taken from the five supplied filings. Figures are in US dollars; the run settings are context, not evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control by Bausch Health, which holds about 87% of the shares and supplies the chairman and interim chief executive, is the main non-financial risk for creditors, because ownership can change through a distribution, sale or foreclosure. The business is diversified across three segments, the issuer has paid no dividend since 2022, and the only debt-funded transfer to the parent in the filings is the USD 2,429 million paid at the listing, funded by new term debt and cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 157–158; 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 258; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation C1; calculation C33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating risk is secondary: Surgical earned USD 18 million of segment profit in 2025 against USD 50 million in 2023, and rebates took 39.5% of gross product sales. The view worsens if the parent draws cash out or control passes to an unknown holder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control is the dominant risk and it is complete. Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, can elect the board, generally decides mergers, financing and dividend policy, and under the separation agreement the issuer needs its written consent for certain significant actions until the parent holds less than 50% of the votes; the issuer qualifies for controlled-company exemptions from board-independence rules. Creditors therefore cannot count on the board to resist the parent on strategy, distributions or acquisitions while control lasts, although related-party dealings need independent-director approval.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leadership is now shared with the parent. The parent's chief executive has chaired the board since August 2026 and became interim chief executive on 2026-10-12, when the former chief executive left under an agreement paying about USD 75 million; the issuer itself names the time demands and conflicts of the dual role as a risk and states no permanent successor. Decisions on strategy, acquisitions and cash can now be taken by one person who answers to both companies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The separation is open-ended and ownership can change on the parent's terms. A distribution depends on the parent reaching targeted debt leverage ratios that are not stated, the parent can terminate the distribution arrangement in its sole discretion, and the agreement's outside date of 2024-12-31 passed without termination. Part of the parent's holding sits in a subsidiary and is pledged for that subsidiary's own 10.00% senior secured notes due 2032, in an amount not stated, so a default there could put an unknown owner in control. Both secured notes give holders a repurchase right at 101% on a change of control; whether the credit agreement has an equivalent is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The record of cash going to the parent is mixed and dated. In 2022 the issuer paid the parent USD 2,200 million to settle an intercompany note and USD 229 million as a return of capital, funded by the new term loan and cash. Since the listing no dividend has been declared or paid, the parent's agreements cost the issuer USD 8 million in 2025, no sales were made to related parties, and a 2022 lawsuit seeking to treat transfers from the parent as voidable and to make the issuer liable for damages awarded against the parent was settled in 2025 and dismissed in January 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 258; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 263–264; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 317–318; calculation C33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating base is broad but concentrated at the edges. Revenue was USD 5,101 million in 2025, up 6.47%, across three segments, with 49.91% earned in the United States and Puerto Rico; yet the top ten products were 56% of revenue against 48% in 2023, two wholesalers are each about 10% of revenue, finished product for six named products comes from a single source, and about 37% of product sales are made wholly or partly by third parties.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 322–323; calculation C24; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Profit rests on Vision Care and on rebate discipline. Vision Care earned USD 849 million of the USD 1,125 million segment profit in 2025 at a 29.05% margin, while the Pharmaceuticals margin fell to 20.09% in 2025 from 28.83% in 2023, with rebates rising to 24.40% of gross product sales in 2025 from 19.90% in 2024, and recovered to 28.17% in the first nine months of 2026, when deductions eased. Surgical earned a 2.01% margin in 2025, in the year of the enVista recall, and 8.08% in the nine months of 2026.

fields.value: - Acquisitions since the 2023 purchase of XIIDRA have been small by comparison, and the pending one has no stated funding. XIIDRA cost USD 1,750 million upfront and was paid from the 2023 secured notes and term loan; deals since January 2025 total about USD 221 million of upfront cash including the pending USD 85 million purchase of surgical manufacturing businesses, whose target, size and funding source the filings do not state. Contingent payments of about USD 242 million are reasonably possible.

fields.value: - Disclosure supports monitoring of the issuer but not analysis of the parent. The statements are audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers with an unqualified opinion and effective internal control, and the one critical audit matter is the Medicaid rebate estimate, with USD 556 million of rebates accrued. Director, pay and related-person information is incorporated from a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the parent's own financial position, the size of the pledge and its leverage target are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Regulatory and quality events have so far been contained. The 2025 enVista recall was followed by a return to pre-recall sales in the fourth quarter of 2025, and the September 2026 FDA warning letter on the Tampa site does not require manufacturing to stop; management says it expects no supply interruption, a statement the filings do not test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against putting control first is the parent's restraint since 2022. Its holding has not changed since 2025-02, no dividend has been paid, related-party dealings are small, the issuer refinanced on 2025-06-26 and 2026-01-02 to move maturities to January 2031, and the board has nine named independent directors with an auditor reporting effective controls. The debt is guaranteed by the issuer's own subsidiaries and the filings name no guarantee by the parent, so no contractual channel from the parent's debt to the issuer's is named in the filings, although ratings can move with the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if a distribution left no controlling shareholder, if a permanent chief executive independent of the parent were appointed, or if the pledge size and the parent's leverage target were disclosed and proved benign. It would worsen on a dividend, an intercompany loan or any other cash call by the parent, on a foreclosure on pledged shares, or on a sale to a holder whose plans differ, and on any rating action driven by the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The parent's own finances, the size of the pledge and the parent's leverage target are outside the five filings, so the likelihood and timing of an ownership change cannot be sized and the control conclusion stays qualitative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Directors' backgrounds, committee membership, pay and the related-person policy sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the conclusion that creditors cannot count on the board to resist the parent rests on the controlled-company disclosure and a list of independent directors alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 222; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment profit is stated before amortization and other expense and no profit is given by product, so the profit-concentration conclusion describes segments and not products.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pending acquisition is described in two sentences without target, size or funding, so its effect on leverage, integration and the acquisition-appetite view is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2022 payments to the parent appear only in the 2024 annual report and not in the later annual report, so the conclusion on cash paid to the parent rests on one dated disclosure that cannot be checked against a later one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Statements that the portfolio is diversified, that acquisitions will raise margins and that supply will not be interrupted are management language and are not tested here, so the business-strength conclusion rests on reported figures only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No single transaction sits at the centre of this credit. The open transaction is the separation from Bausch Health, announced on 2020-08-06 and not completed: a distribution depends on the parent reaching leverage targets that the filings do not state, the parent can end the arrangement at its sole discretion, the agreement's outside date of 2024-12-31 passed without termination, and a sale or a transfer to the parent's shareholders remains possible. No date is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one large acquisition since the listing was XIIDRA from Novartis, signed on 2023-06-30 and completed on 2023-09-29 for USD 1,750 million upfront plus potential milestones of up to USD 750 million, paid from USD 1,400 million of 8.375% secured notes due October 2028 and a new term loan. Later deals were small: Whitecap Biosciences for about USD 28 million on 2025-01-03, two acquisitions for about USD 33 million in November 2025 and Mexican manufacturing assets for about USD 75 million on 2025-12-09. On 2026-10-08 the issuer agreed to buy ophthalmic surgical manufacturing businesses for about USD 85 million of upfront cash, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026; the filings do not name the target, size it or state how the cash will be funded. The separation agreement with the former chief executive adds a lump-sum payment of about USD 75 million, payable under that agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues since the listing have been refinancings. On 2022-05-10 the issuer took a USD 2,500 million term loan and a USD 500 million revolver; the term loan proceeds and cash paid the parent USD 2,429 million. It added USD 1,400 million of secured notes and USD 500 million of term loans on 2023-09-29 to buy XIIDRA and USD 400 million of term loans on 2024-11-01. On 2025-06-26 it replaced the 2027 maturities with a USD 800 million revolver due 2030, a USD 2,325 million term loan due 2031 and EUR 675 million of floating rate notes due 2031, and on 2026-01-02 it refinanced the 2028 and 2031 term loans into a USD 2,802 million term loan due 2031-01-15 to extend maturities and lower the rate. At 2026-09-30 principal outstanding was USD 5,065 million, or USD 5,017 million net of USD 48 million of unamortized discounts and issuance costs: the term loan USD 2,788 million, the 2028 notes USD 1,400 million, the 2031 notes USD 765 million, the revolver USD 100 million and other debt USD 12 million. The credit facilities and both note series are secured by the same first-priority liens, the notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the credit agreement and carry a 101% repurchase right on a change of control, and the revolver has a springing first lien net leverage test of 5.75x stepping down to 5.00x that applies only when more than 35% of the USD 800 million commitments are drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: ready with limitations. The five filings support the business, ownership and governance facts, but no filing of the parent, no proxy statement and no executed debt document was supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by concentrated parent control, pledged shares and shared leadership, because they let ownership and strategy change without creditor consent, which implies event risk for the debt. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends since 2022, small related-party charges and audited disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: the number of issuer shares pledged and the terms of the 10.00% Senior Secured Notes due 2032 of the parent's subsidiary. It limits the ownership and control conclusion, because the filings state only that a portion is pledged, so they cannot show how close a foreclosure and a change of control are. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the parent's annual report and the indenture of those notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: the parent's targeted debt leverage ratios for a distribution and its current leverage against them. It limits the separation-timing conclusion, because the distribution is conditional on these targets and without them its timing and likelihood cannot be judged. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the parent's leverage disclosure and any statement of the targets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: director biographies, committee membership, executive pay, related-person policy and beneficial ownership table. It limits the board-independence conclusion, because independence and incentives cannot be assessed beyond a named list of independent directors. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: change-of-control, restricted-payment, investment and affiliate-transaction terms of the credit agreement and the indentures. It limits the assessment of legal capacity for dividends, loans to the parent or asset transfers, because only the 101% note repurchase right is stated, so that capacity cannot be measured. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the executed credit agreement and indentures, which the annual report lists as exhibits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: target, size, price basis and funding source of the pending USD 85 million surgical manufacturing acquisition. It limits the acquisition-appetite view, because funding from cash or the revolver changes liquidity, and the pattern of small acquisitions cannot be extended without it. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain the announcement and the closing report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: payment date and other terms of the former chief executive's USD 75 million lump sum and any similar executive arrangements. It limits the assessment of executive payments, because the payment falls in the fourth quarter on the company's own cash-needs list but its date is not stated. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain the separation agreement or the related current report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: revenue and profit by product beyond the top-ten share and the PreserVision share, and wholesaler contract terms. It limits the concentration conclusion, because concentration can be sized only by shares of the total. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain product revenue disclosure and distribution agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: amounts by agreement under the separation agreements and the terms of the intellectual property and real estate agreements with the parent. It limits the assessment of related-party leakage, because only aggregate charges are stated, so leakage through shared assets cannot be excluded. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain the agreements and the related-party schedule.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: lender reporting package: compliance certificates, covenant ratios and basket usage. It limits the monitoring assessment, because the filings state compliance without a ratio, so lender monitoring cannot be tested. Severity Minor; the action is to request the compliance certificate and basket tracker from the agent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: identity of the noncontrolling interest holders and the subsidiaries concerned. It limits the ownership register, because minority claims at subsidiary level can rank ahead of the issuer's creditors on those assets. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain subsidiary list and note disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: holdings of directors and officers and any shareholder agreement other than the separation agreements. It limits the ownership register, because alignment of management with the parent or with public holders cannot be judged. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: fee, term and role under the consulting agreement dated 2026-08-06 between the issuer and a director named independent in the 2025 annual report. It limits the board-independence conclusion, because payments to a director can affect independence tests and only the exhibit title is stated. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain exhibit 10.1 of the third-quarter report and the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.value: | 5 | Liquidity and a dormant covenant | Liquidity of USD 1,179 million is 3.30x the USD 357 million of fourth-quarter needs; USD 100 million of the USD 800 million revolver is drawn; the first lien net leverage test applies only above USD 280 million of loans | Cash and revolver cover the stated calls, and USD 180 million of room remains before the only maintenance test applies | Lowers liquidity-driven default risk through 2027; the covenant ratio itself is not established | Positive | Medium | Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C45; calculation C48; calculation C49 |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 6 | Pricing, rebates and generic entry | Deductions were 39.5% of gross product sales in 2025, up 3.2 percentage points, and 38.4% in nine months of 2026 against 39.1% a year earlier; net pricing was 40.38% of nine-month revenue growth; Lumify generic entry is allowed from 2027-06-30 or earlier; the ten largest products are 56% of revenue | Net price depends on rebates and policy, and a generic entrant removes both volume and pricing from a top product | Revenue and margin are exposed in the window before the 2028 refinancing; the size of the Lumify exposure is not established | Negative | Medium | 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; calculation C54; calculation C39 |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 7 | Operating breadth and growth | Three segments each grew in 2025; revenue grew 10.03%, 15.56% and 6.47% in 2023, 2024 and 2025 and 8.58% in nine months of 2026; two wholesalers account for about 10% of revenue each | Demand is spread across product lines and regions and both price and volume added to growth | A single-product failure would not by itself stop debt service, although concentration in the ten largest products limits that comfort | Positive | Medium | Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79 |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 8 | Supply and quality concentration | Finished product for six named products is single-sourced, about 37% of product sales are made wholly or partly by third parties, a September 2026 FDA warning letter covers the Tampa site, and Surgical earned USD 18 million of segment profit in 2025 | An interruption removes revenue from products with no second source, and the 2025 enVista recall cut Surgical profit | A tail risk to earnings that has been contained so far; management states it expects no supply interruption | Negative | Low | 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65 |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bausch & Lomb Corp (reporting as Bausch + Lomb Corporation and its subsidiaries; issuer id blco-1860742), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the overall fundamental credit view, its strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside, drawn from the five supplied filings and the three earlier handoffs. Figures are in US dollars; the run settings are context, not evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is weak but improving: total debt of 6.47x last-twelve-month EBITDA, interest cover of 2.05x on accrued expense and control by Bausch Health leave creditors reliant on one year of earnings recovery holding until the 2028 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a three-segment eye-health franchise with revenue of USD 5,418 million over the last twelve months, and net pricing supplied 40.38% of the nine-month revenue increase. Liquidity of USD 1,179 million and no maturity beyond amortization before 2028 buy time, but net leverage of 5.82x at 2026-09-30 becomes 5.93x pro forma for the acquisition agreed on 2026-10-08 and 5.92x pro forma for the executive payment under the separation agreement dated 2026-10-11. The main downside is earnings falling back, through rebates, generic competition or supply problems, before the 2028 notes are refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage has fallen but remains high, and it fell because earnings rose, not because debt fell. Total debt of USD 5,095 million is 6.47x last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 787 million, against 9.52x at FY2025, while debt itself is higher than at FY2025. EBITDA rose 47.38%, but USD 62 million of non-cash inventory step-up amortization sat in the FY2025 base, so the like-for-like rise is 32.05%. Because leverage is a ratio to one year of earnings, a return of EBITDA to its FY2025 level, a fall of 32.15%, would put total debt at 9.54x EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest cover is thin and the debt is mostly floating, so a rate shock and an earnings shock would arrive together. Accrued interest of USD 383 million takes 48.67% of EBITDA, cash interest cover was 1.41x in FY2025 and cannot be measured for the latest twelve months, and 72.12% of principal pays a floating rate with no interest rate swap or cap described in the filings. A rise of 100 bp adds about USD 36.53 million a year and takes cover from 2.05x to 1.88x; at the FY2025 earnings level cover would be 1.39x, or 1.27x after the same rise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion has turned positive but is still modest. Last-twelve-month free cash flow of USD 252 million is 32.02% of EBITDA and 4.95% of total debt, after deficits of USD 198 million, USD 59 million and USD 66 million in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025. Trade receivables absorbed USD 496 million over those three years, more than the cumulative deficit of USD 323 million, so working capital, not the operating margin alone, decides whether the recovery in free cash flow lasts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate for the next year, and the pressure sits in 2028 and 2031. Liquidity of USD 1,179 million is 3.30x the USD 357 million of fourth-quarter needs the issuer lists. Nothing but amortization is due before 2028, when USD 1,440 million falls due, 28.43% of principal and 1.83x EBITDA; USD 3,434 million, 67.80% of principal and 4.36x EBITDA, falls due in 2031. At the FY2025 earnings level those multiples would be 2.70x and 6.43x, so the 2028 notes are the first test of market access and the swing factor from 2027.
