fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The revolver covenant is dormant and leaves room, but it is the only maintenance test and its headroom cannot be measured. The first lien net leverage test of 5.75x, stepping down to 5.50x, 5.25x and then 5.00x in later periods, applies only when revolver loans exceed 35% of the USD 800 million commitment, that is USD 280 million; USD 100 million is drawn, 12.50% of commitments, leaving USD 180 million before the test applies. Even if the USD 85 million acquisition and the USD 75 million executive payment were both drawn in full, loans would be USD 260 million, USD 20 million below the line, so the test is unlikely to apply in the fourth quarter but headroom beyond that is thin, and the issuer states compliance without a ratio so the result of a test is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C48; calculation C49; calculation C52; calculation C50; calculation C51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control by the parent is the main non-financial risk and has a direct liquidity link. Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, and part of its holding is pledged in a subsidiary for that subsidiary's 10.00% notes due 2032, in an amount the filings do not state. A change of control would let holders of both secured notes require repurchase at 101% of principal, USD 2,186.65 million before accrued interest or 1.85x liquidity; whether the credit agreement carries a comparable trigger is not stated, so the exposure of the largest debt, the term loan, is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; calculation C46; calculation C47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pricing and rebates carry the revenue base and are exposed to regulation and generic entry. Net pricing contributed USD 128 million of the USD 317 million nine-month revenue increase and volume USD 139 million, but deductions from gross product sales rose 3.2 percentage points to 39.5% in 2025 and were 38.4% in the nine months of 2026 against 39.1% a year earlier, and a settlement with a generic maker allows entry for Lumify drops from 2027-06-30 or earlier. The ten largest products were 56% of 2025 revenue, up from 48% in 2023, and Lumify revenue is not stated, so the size of the 2027 exposure is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C37; calculation C54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The recovery leans on Pharmaceuticals and on a depressed 2025 base. Pharmaceuticals supplied 56.31% of the USD 293 million rise in nine-month segment profit, helped by lower launch spending and the end of XIIDRA inventory step-up, and Surgical went from USD 3 million to USD 58 million with premium lens growth and the 2025 enVista recall dropping out of the comparison. These are base effects and launch maturity, so the nine-month gain should not be extrapolated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation C16; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Supply and quality concentrations are tail risks that have so far been contained. Finished product for six named products comes from a single source and about 37% of product sales are made wholly or partly by third parties, and a September 2026 FDA warning letter covers the Tampa site without requiring manufacturing to stop; management expects no supply interruption, a statement the filings do not test. A supply failure would remove revenue from products with no second source and would fall on a cost base the analysis treats as largely fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a weak view is that the improvement is broad and cash-backed. EBITDA rose 47.38%, price and volume both contributed in Vision Care and Pharmaceuticals, accrued interest fell 11.76% in nine months, last-twelve-month free cash flow is USD 252 million after three years of deficits, total debt to EBITDA fell from 9.52x to 6.47x, liquidity covers the fourth-quarter needs by 3.30x, and nothing but amortization falls due before 2028. The parent has received no dividend since the listing, and the only large transfer to it in the filings, USD 2,429 million in 2022, is a dated event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation C11; calculation C6; calculation C45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move toward adequate if four quarters keep last-twelve-month EBITDA at or above USD 787 million, if cash interest paid confirms cover near the 2.05x proxy, if the acquisition and the executive payment are met from cash without a revolver draw above USD 180 million, and if the 2028 notes are refinanced ahead of maturity. It would weaken if rebates return toward the 2025 level, if Lumify generic entry is accelerated, if the revolver is drawn past the 35% line, or if the parent takes cash out or its pledged shares are foreclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C8; calculation C49

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest cover and the rate sensitivity at 2026-09-30 are this analysis's own constructions from the debt table, accrued expense and the year-end sensitivity, because the quarterly filing gives no floating-rate split or cash interest, so the conclusion on interest burden is an estimate and not an issuer statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer data, rating-agency view or market pricing was supplied, so the judgement that the financial profile is weak rests on absolute metrics and the issuer's own history, and not on a comparison with similar issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lumify generic entry is dated but the product's revenue and the settlement's acceleration terms are not stated, so the conclusion that revenue durability is moderate cannot size the 2027 loss of exclusivity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fall of EBITDA to its FY2025 level is a reference point and not a forecast, because no management projection or guidance was supplied, so the downside conclusion states direction and sensitivity but no probability or timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maintenance and growth capital spending are not split and only the year-end capital commitment is stated, so the conclusion that capex gives the issuer a lever in a downturn is not established and the cash-conversion view assumes the latest level continues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and the covenant definitions were not supplied, so the conclusion that the revolver test is dormant rests on the drawn share of commitments alone and says nothing about the ratio itself.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Five strengths and five weaknesses carry the view, each ranked by its weight in the credit judgement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength 1: earnings and cash flow have recovered. Last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 787 million compares with USD 534 million for FY2025, a like-for-like rise of 32.05% after the inventory step-up charge is removed from the base, and free cash flow of USD 252 million follows three years of deficits. Free cash flow now exceeds the term loan amortization of USD 28 million a year several times over, which lowers the chance that the revolver funds interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength 2: liquidity and the maturity profile give time. Liquidity of USD 1,179 million is 3.30x the fourth-quarter needs the issuer lists, nothing but amortization falls due before 2028, and the revolver runs to 2030, so a refinancing event is not forced inside the next 12 months and the revolver test applies only above USD 280 million of loans.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C45; calculation C48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength 3: the operating base has three segments and none shrank. In 2025 Vision Care earned USD 2,923 million of revenue, Pharmaceuticals USD 1,284 million and Surgical USD 894 million, and revenue grew in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025, so a setback in one product line does not by itself threaten debt service, although the ten largest products are 56% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength 4: price and volume both added to growth. In nine months net pricing added USD 128 million and volume USD 139 million to revenue, which shows demand holding at higher prices and supports margin recovery, provided rebates stay contained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C36; calculation C37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength 5: the parent has so far left cash in the issuer. No dividend has been paid since the listing and related-party charges were USD 8 million in 2025, which means no recurring leakage to the parent appears in the record, although control remains a risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 263; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 264

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness 1: leverage is high and interest cover is thin. Total debt is 6.47x EBITDA and accrued interest takes 48.67% of EBITDA, so the issuer has little room if earnings slip, and cash interest cover was 1.41x in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness 2: the parent controls the issuer and part of its stake is pledged. A foreclosure or private sale could bring a new controller, and holders of both secured notes could then demand USD 2,186.65 million, 1.85x liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; calculation C46; calculation C47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness 3: the maturities are concentrated and mostly floating. USD 1,440 million falls due in 2028 and USD 3,434 million in 2031, 67.80% of principal, while 72.12% of principal pays a floating rate, so refinancing terms and rate moves land on the same debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C44; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness 4: revenue depends on pricing and on products near loss of exclusivity. Deductions from gross sales were 39.5% in 2025, up 3.2 percentage points, net pricing was 40.38% of nine-month growth, and Lumify faces generic entry from 2027-06-30 or earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C54; calculation C39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness 5: supply and quality are concentrated. Six named products depend on a single finished-product source and Surgical earned only USD 18 million of segment profit in 2025, so a quality event reaches earnings quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bausch + Lomb sells contact lenses and lens care, over-the-counter eye drops, prescription eye medicines and surgical equipment, implants and consumables. In 2025 Vision Care was 57.30% of revenue at USD 2,923 million, Pharmaceuticals 25.17% at USD 1,284 million and Surgical 17.53% at USD 894 million, and the United States and Puerto Rico supplied 49.91%. The analysis reads repeat purchase of lenses, solutions and drops by consumers and eye-care professionals as giving the revenue base visibility, which supports cash-flow predictability and debt service, but the ten largest products and franchises were 56% of revenue against 48% in 2023, so the visibility is concentrated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth has been partly bought. XIIDRA was acquired in 2023 for USD 1,750 million upfront and paid for with the October 2028 notes and a new term loan, which is the origin of the 2028 maturity; deals since January 2025 total about USD 221 million of upfront cash including the pending USD 85 million purchase of surgical manufacturing businesses, and the issuer says it regularly considers acquisitions, some of which could be sizable. Acquisition appetite therefore competes with debt reduction for cash, and the pending purchase has no stated funding source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 269; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 270; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bausch Health holds about 87% of the shares, can elect the board and generally decides mergers, financing and dividend policy, and the issuer needs its written consent for certain significant actions until it holds less than 50% of the votes; the issuer qualifies for controlled-company exemptions from board-independence rules. Creditors therefore cannot count on the board to resist the parent on leverage, acquisitions or distributions, and financial policy is set by a shareholder whose own finances are not in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor claims are structured conservatively. The credit facilities and notes are secured by substantially all assets of the issuer and its material wholly owned Canadian, U.S., Dutch and Irish subsidiaries, the notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the credit agreement and rank equally with the facilities, and they are structurally behind liabilities of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them. The issuer does not guarantee the parent's debt, so the parent's creditors have no direct claim on it, although a downgrade of the parent could still lower the issuer's ratings and raise its cost of debt. Noncontrolling interests of USD 71 million can rank ahead of the issuer's creditors on the assets they own.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 192; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The separation is an open option for the parent and not a plan. A distribution depends on the parent reaching targeted debt leverage ratios that are not stated, the parent can terminate the arrangement in its sole discretion, and the outside date of 2024-12-31 passed without termination. The leadership now overlaps: the parent's chief executive has chaired the issuer's board since August 2026 and has been interim chief executive since 2026-10-12, when the former chief executive left under an agreement paying about USD 75 million. Decisions on strategy, acquisitions and cash can therefore be taken by one person who answers to both companies, which raises the weight of the pledge and change-of-control exposure described above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 103

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The analysis reads revenue as mostly repeat consumer and clinician demand, and it is growing. In the nine months of 2026 over-the-counter products were USD 1,418 million and devices USD 1,521 million of USD 4,013 million, prescription pharmaceuticals USD 885 million and branded and other generics USD 175 million, and revenue rose 8.58%, or 7.28% excluding foreign exchange. Revenue also grew in each of the last three years, by 10.03% in 2023, 15.56% in 2024 and 6.47% in 2025, which supports the view that debt service rests on a growing base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Price is a large part of that growth and is the most exposed. Net pricing added USD 128 million, volume USD 139 million and foreign exchange USD 48 million to the USD 317 million increase, so pricing was 40.38% of it, with Surgical pricing negative by USD 3 million and Surgical growth driven by volume. In the United States the Inflation Reduction Act requires manufacturers to pay Medicare rebates when prices rise faster than inflation, and deductions from gross product sales were 39.5% in 2025, up 3.2 percentage points, and were 38.4% in the nine months of 2026 against 39.1% a year earlier. A return of rebates would reduce net sales without any fall in volume, so revenue durability is moderate and sensitive to policy and to rebate contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C37; calculation C38; calculation C39; calculation C54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration is the second risk. Two wholesalers each account for about 10% of revenue, the ten largest products rose to 56% of 2025 revenue, and a 2025 settlement lets a generic maker enter the market for Lumify drops from 2027-06-30 or earlier. The filings state that the loss of exclusivity risk is limited over five years and that PreserVision, about 6% of revenue, is an over-the-counter product whose method-of-use patent expired in early 2026, with a smaller expected effect than a branded drug. Lumify revenue is not stated, so the loss of exclusivity inside the 2028 refinancing window cannot be sized and revenue visibility beyond 2027 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 175; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 176; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have widened because costs were held while revenue grew, which is real operating leverage but not yet proven in a downturn. Nine-month selling, general and administrative cost rose 1.08% against revenue growth of 8.58%, cost of goods sold fell as a share of product sales to 37.4% from 41.1% on mix, currency, the end of the 2025 XIIDRA step-up and enVista recall effects and USD 15 million of tariff recoveries, and EBITDA margin rose 4.06 percentage points to 14.53% from 10.47% in FY2025. Selling, general and administrative cost was 43.80% of FY2025 revenue and the analysis treats it as largely fixed in the short run, so a revenue fall would cut margin faster than revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 236; calculation C34; calculation C53; calculation C33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The margin gain contains items that will not repeat and others that can be reversed. The USD 15 million of tariff recoveries and the end of the step-up are one-off, advertising and promotion fell because XIIDRA and MIEBO left their launch phase, and research and development rose 10% to USD 306 million in nine months. Reported EBITDA is also unadjusted: it is after other expense, net of USD 127 million over the last twelve months and after share-based compensation, so it is a conservative base. The levers available in a downturn are advertising and promotion, research and development timing and the cost programs the issuer says it may start, which together give some cost flexibility but not enough to hold margin if gross-to-net deductions rise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 90; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is positive but only 32.02% of EBITDA, because interest, capital spending and working capital absorb the rest. Operating cash flow was USD 554 million over the last twelve months, 70.39% of EBITDA, and capital expenditure was USD 302 million, 5.57% of revenue, down from 6.84% in FY2025. Cash interest paid was USD 380 million in FY2025 against EBITDA of USD 534 million and income taxes paid USD 59 million, which shows that interest is the largest fixed claim on cash. Trade receivables take cash as revenue grows: receivable days were 73.86 days at the end of FY2023, 87.37 days at FY2025 and 77.27 days at 2026-09-30. The issuer attributes the nine-month rise in operating cash flow to higher operating results, partly offset by the timing of payments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 235; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 308; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2024-12-31_blco_blco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 225; calculation C24; calculation C23; calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is the main flexible cash item, but its flexibility is not established. The issuer lists about USD 60 million of capital spending for the fourth quarter and had capital commitments of USD 128 million at year-end 2025, and it does not split maintenance from growth spending. The receivables sale facility signed in January 2026 produced only USD 26 million of proceeds in nine months, all collected by quarter-end, so it is a small and optional source of liquidity and not a driver of the cash flow shown. Cash available for debt reduction after interest is therefore limited to the last-twelve-month free cash flow, and the term loan amortization is only USD 28 million a year, so deleveraging has to come from earnings growth. Claims outside the debt figure add to fixed charges: operating lease liabilities of USD 163 million and a net pension and retiree deficit of USD 31 million at 2025-12-31 sit outside total debt, while USD 78 million of failed sale-leaseback obligations sit inside it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 292; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 297; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 319; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rivalry is high and is fought on price, efficacy and marketing. The issuer competes with large pharmaceutical and device companies, over-the-counter companies, generic makers and smaller regional firms, and the analysis reads that as keeping advertising and promotion high to defend share, which caps how much margin can be released in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The threat of new entrants is concentrated in generic entry. A settlement lets a generic maker enter the market for Lumify drops from 2027-06-30 or earlier and other generic makers have filed applications, while the issuer states that the expiry of about 22 US patents in 2026, 37 in 2027 and 26 in 2028 is not expected to have a material adverse effect, so erosion risk is real but concentrated in a few products in the same window as the 2028 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Substitution between product forms and between prescription and over-the-counter treatments is not measured in the filings, so the substitute force is not established; the one stated substitution channel is generic and authorized-generic entry, covered above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Buyer and payor power is the main margin swing. Two wholesalers are each about 10% of revenue, group purchasing contracts and legislation restrict price increases, and chargebacks rose to 8.70% of gross sales in nine months from 7.50% while rebates fell to 22.10% from 23.80%, so net sales depend on contracts and policy more than on volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Supplier power is high for named products. Finished product for six named products and the active ingredient for four are single-sourced and about 37% of product sales are made wholly or partly by third parties, so a supplier failure interrupts revenue with no second source and cannot be offset by cost cuts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Regulation and policy are material because they act directly on net price. Pricing is restricted by group purchasing contracts and by law: the Inflation Reduction Act requires Medicare rebates when prices rise faster than inflation, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act restricts funding of government health programs and may lower reimbursement, and a May 2025 executive order on most-favored-nation pricing may affect branded pharmaceutical products, while the issuer says the effect of expected health care changes is unclear, so policy can lower net sales and margin together across the United States, which is 49.91% of revenue, and regional spread elsewhere does not offset it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 175; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 322

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Tariffs and trade policy are material but have so far helped: the issuer recorded USD 15 million of recoveries of previously paid tariffs in nine months, a one-off gain that flatters margin, while it remains exposed to further tariffs on imported and exported product.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest rates and currency are material through the debt. A majority of revenue and expense is in US dollars, but euro notes with principal of USD 765 million float on EURIBOR, a 1% move in foreign exchange rates changes equity by about USD 23 million, and cross-currency swaps of USD 1,000 million are described as hedging euro net investment, not interest rates. Russia, Ukraine and Belarus together were about 3% of revenue and the affected Middle East regions about 2%, a small and monitored exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 219; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Social and technology factors are not a primary credit driver on the filings supplied; the pipeline setback in July 2026, when the Phase 2 glaucoma neuroprotection trial missed its primary endpoint, removes upside but no cash flow that supports debt today.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strengths: recovering EBITDA and positive free cash flow, liquidity of USD 1,179 million, no maturity before 2028 beyond amortization, three segments with growth in each, and price and volume both contributing to growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weaknesses: total debt at 6.47x EBITDA, accrued interest at 48.67% of EBITDA, 72.12% of principal at floating rates, control by a parent with a pledged stake, and ten products at 56% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Opportunities that would improve credit quality: the October 2028 notes have been callable since 2025-10-01 so they can be refinanced when markets allow, product mix has lowered cost of goods sold as a share of product sales and may continue to, and a distribution that ended parent control could remove the pledge and change-of-control exposure, although its terms are not known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Threats that would weaken it: generic entry for Lumify from 2027-06-30, rebates returning toward 2025 levels, a foreclosure on pledged shares, a rating action on the parent, an FDA escalation at the Tampa site and a debt-funded acquisition following the pending purchase.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is weak and improving, and the business profile is average. Scale is a support: revenue of USD 5,418 million over the last twelve months across three segments, with growth in each of the last three years. The constraints are leverage of 6.47x, cash interest cover of 1.41x in FY2025, a floating share of principal of 72.12%, free cash flow that was negative for three years until the last twelve months, and financial policy set by a controlling parent. The trend is up: EBITDA margin moved to 14.53% from 10.47%, and leverage fell from 9.52x to 6.47x, but both gains are one year old and partly reflect a depressed 2025 base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The datapoints that would make the view more definitive are cash interest paid for 2026, an issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA and covenant ratio, the size of the pledged stake and the parent's leverage target, Lumify revenue, and the maintenance share of capital spending. Refinancing capacity is average: the issuer refinanced to 2030 and 2031 in June 2025 and January 2026, but USD 1,440 million falls due in 2028 and market access depends on earnings holding and on the parent's standing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Over the next one to two years, tailwinds are the earnings run-rate and lower interest: third-quarter operating income was USD 155 million against USD 95 million a year earlier and third-quarter interest expense was USD 95 million against USD 101 million. These support cover and cash generation if they persist.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Headwinds over the same period are the fourth-quarter cash calls of USD 357 million, the leadership transition, generic entry for Lumify from 2027-06-30, and an FDA warning letter for the Tampa site. Together they test whether free cash flow can fund the pending acquisition and the executive payment without drawing the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 89

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Over three to five years, the debt profile decides the outcome: USD 1,440 million in 2028 and USD 3,434 million in 2031 must be refinanced from an earnings base of USD 787 million, or deleveraged from free cash flow of USD 252 million a year at the current rate. Health care pricing reform and generic competition are the sector headwinds that bear on that base; the issuer expects loss of exclusivity risk to be limited over five years but says it could change through patent challenges, settlements and at-risk launches.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Company-specific tailwinds are the maturing launches of XIIDRA and MIEBO and premium intraocular lens growth; the pipeline is a weaker support after the July 2026 Phase 2 setback, so growth must come from existing products.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside scenario is a fall of EBITDA back to its FY2025 level of USD 534 million, a drop of 32.15%, used as a reference point and not as a forecast. The initiating condition is a combination the filings make plausible: rebates and deductions return toward their 2025 level of 39.5% of gross product sales, Lumify faces generic entry from 2027-06-30 or earlier, and a supply or quality problem hits a single-source product. The first operating break is net revenue and margin, because pricing supplied 40.38% of nine-month growth and the analysis treats selling and administrative cost as largely fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 180–181; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C17; calculation C39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission is through leverage and cover before liquidity. At the FY2025 earnings level total debt would be 9.54x EBITDA and accrued interest cover 1.39x, or 1.27x after a 100 bp rise, and the 2028 and 2031 maturities would be 2.70x and 6.43x EBITDA. FY2025 itself produced negative free cash flow of USD 66 million, so liquidity of USD 1,179 million would fund the shortfall for a long time and the revolver covenant, which applies only above USD 280 million of loans, would not bind unless loans rose by more than USD 180 million. The break therefore comes at refinancing: the 2028 notes would have to be replaced when EBITDA and cover are weakest, at a rate the market sets, and if the parent came under pressure, cash could be called on or pledged shares foreclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 219; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C48; calculation C49

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management levers are advertising and promotion, research and development timing, capital spending of USD 302 million over the last twelve months against capital commitments of USD 128 million, cost programs the issuer says it may start, the receivables facility and sale-leaseback of property, and the USD 666 million of revolver availability. These make liquidity distress unlikely before 2028 on the evidence, but they do not restore refinancing capacity at the downside leverage, and no default is assumed. Primary downside path: earnings fall back through rebates, generic entry or supply failure while the 2028 notes approach maturity and the parent holds control. The observable triggers are listed in the monitoring register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_blco_blco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 319

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Bausch + Lomb presents an adequate business profile supported by a three-segment product range, repeat consumer and clinician demand and growth in each of the last three years, but credit quality is constrained by total debt of 6.47x EBITDA, thin interest cover, a mostly floating debt structure and control by a parent with a pledged stake. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but unproven: free cash flow of USD 252 million is one year old and rests on pricing and a depressed 2025 base. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings holding above USD 787 million, on rebates staying contained and on the parent not taking cash or losing control before the 2028 notes mature. Business quality compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers in eye health is not established, because no peer data were supplied. Further analysis would require cash interest paid for 2026, the credit agreement and covenant definitions, the size of the pledge and Lumify revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_blco_blco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: a fall in earnings through rebates, generic entry or supply failure while leverage is high and the 2028 notes are refinanced under parent control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: ready with limitations. The five filings and the findings of three earlier modules support the fundamental view, but no proxy statement, parent filing, credit agreement or peer data was supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: cash interest paid for the nine months of 2026 and the latest twelve months. It limits the interest-cover conclusion, because the filings print cash interest only for full years, so cover is measured on accrued expense, which differed from cash paid by USD 41 million in FY2025. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the cash flow supplement of the next annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: the credit agreement, its covenant definitions and any change-of-control or default terms for the term loan. It limits the conclusion on the revolver test and on the term loan's exposure to a change of control, because the largest debt, USD 2,788 million, has no stated change-of-control term and the covenant ratio cannot be calculated. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the executed credit agreement and a compliance certificate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: peer leverage, credit ratings and market pricing. It limits the comparison of the financial profile with similar issuers, because the weak judgement rests on absolute metrics and the issuer's own history, not on a peer set. Severity Material; the action is to obtain peer, rating and bond price data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: Lumify revenue and the acceleration clauses of the 2025 settlement. It limits the revenue-durability conclusion, because the loss of exclusivity from 2027-06-30 cannot be sized. Severity Material; the action is to obtain product revenue and the settlement terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: the size of the pledged parent shares and the parent's leverage target. It limits the conclusion on control and change-of-control risk, because the likelihood and timing of an ownership change cannot be judged. Severity Material; the action is to obtain the parent's filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: the split between maintenance and growth capital spending. It limits the assessment of capex flexibility, because the lever available in a downturn cannot be sized. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain the issuer's capital allocation disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: management projections or guidance. It limits the downside and outlook sections, because the reference fall in EBITDA has no stated probability or timing. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain issuer guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Not supplied: an issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA. It limits the leverage conclusion, because reported EBITDA is after other expense, net of USD 127 million over the last twelve months and no issuer bridge exists. Severity Minor; the action is to obtain the issuer's covenant earnings definition.

fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.
